links.comparator_used: Original AHA-PREVENT equations applied as-is to the local population (also compared with a traditional recalibration approach)
links.outcome: Calibration (modified Hosmer-Lemeshow) in the test set; also discrimination (Harrell C index) and risk reclassification
links.effect: MLM-PREVENT was better calibrated overall (χ23 = 2.2; P = .53 vs χ23 > 16.3; P < .001), in men (χ23 = 2.1; P = .55 vs χ23 > 16.3; P < .001) and in women (χ23 = 6.5; P = .09 vs χ23 > 16.3; P < .001). It also surpassed traditional recalibration. Discrimination was equal (approximate ΔC index, ±0.01). At the 7.5% risk threshold, 11.5% of patients were reclassified.
links.quote: The interpretable ML approach presented in this article enhanced the accuracy of the AHA-PREVENT model when applied to a local population while still preserving the risk associations found by the original model.

design_hint: local recalibration of risk model before deployment
